checks.ab: 27B against the stock build's bf16 reference (EQUALITY-27B.md, VTP43.md): long-corpus mean KLD bf16_i8 0.002685 and bf16_fp8 0.003228 against fp8 0.004947 (bar 0.0027 met by bf16_i8), short 0.001411 and 0.001922 against fp8 0.002235; capacity 1.31x and 1.34x bf16; decode at 1, 4 and 8 streams and TTFT within 3% of fp8 (VTP43.md). Flash-Next (FLASHNEXT-AB.md, single runs, two XTX, no helper, no speculation): decode and TTFT within about 1% of bf16 for bf16_i8, bf16_fp8 +6.7% on one-stream decode and 5.9% slower 48K TTFT; capacity 1.283x (bf16_i8) and 1.307x (bf16_fp8) of bf16 because the QSA block-key cache is not quantised; needle probe at 48K tokens 9 of 9 and 8 of 9 against 8 of 9 for bf16; Flash-Next KLD against bf16 sits inside the model's arithmetic-noise band (re-chunking the bf16 cache alone gives the same) so it cannot judge KV error (FLASHNEXT-KLD.md); the R9700 helper arm was not run.
checks.activation: `--kv-cache-dtype bf16_i8` or `bf16_fp8` selects the packed layout from the one layout table: the engine reports the layout and sizes pages from it (Flash-Next attention page 36.75 and 36.00 KiB against 48.00 KiB for bf16, FLASHNEXT-AB.md; 27B 818,896 and 835,952 tokens against 624,048 for bf16, VTP43.md); an unsupported (layout, head_dim, gqa) refuses at startup naming the tuple; the default caches are selected exactly as before.
checks.identity: the default caches are unchanged: against references the stock build recorded, the patched build scores Flash-Next bf16 6.4e-11 and fp8 3.3e-11 mean KLD with top-1 100% over 4,161 positions (IDENTITY.md), and 27B bf16 6.1e-11 and fp8 4.7e-11 on the short corpus (42,761 positions) and bf16 4.8e-11 on the long one (276,900), top-1 100% (EQUALITY-27B.md); at the tool's float floor, not bit-exact (two binaries); the packed caches differ from bf16 by design and are measured in the A/B line.
